A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NoLiMa benchmark. The main text, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and retained appendix material.

before.justification: V2 reports original model evaluations, reasoning-model experiments, and CoT and literal-match ablations, including Tables 3–6.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds newer-model evaluations, longer-context tests, and detailed one-hop and two-hop results in Tables 10–12.

M1.justification: The needle templates, latent-hop and inverted-order construction, filtering pipeline, and prompting procedures are retained. Section 3.1 clarifies and renames filtering of unintended answer candidates without documenting a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix E extends actual evaluation from a maximum of 32K tokens to 64K and 128K, introducing longer input-context scenarios. The underlying filtered books, needle sets, and task requirements remain the same.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Gemini 2.0 Flash. Table 10 additionally evaluates GPT-4.1, Mini and Nano; Gemini 2.5 Flash; Llama 4 Maverick and Scout; and Gemma 3 at 4B, 12B and 27B. These ten additions substantially expand the evaluated model set while retaining the earlier models and reasoning comparators.

E3.justification: For the added long-context evaluation, Appendix E specifies 11 needle placements instead of the default 26 and 127,500-token haystacks for nominal 128K tests of GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash. Appendix F computes base scores and thresholds separately for each hop subset. The original main evaluation protocol is retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F extends the existing investigation of reasoning-hop difficulty with detailed one-hop and two-hop results across all thirteen main-table models, beyond the earlier two-model plot and Llama CoT breakdown. The original inversion, placement-depth, distractor, and literal-match analyses remain.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged. Both versions average over five haystacks and provide no confidence intervals or significance tests. The added unsmoothed depth curves display existing positional variation rather than statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V3 substantially expands numerical results through Table 10's newer-model and 64K/128K evaluations and Tables 11–12's per-hop breakdowns. Newly reported 128K accuracies include GPT-4o at 56.0% and GPT-4.1 at 64.7%. Some retained Table 3 values also change, such as Command R+ at 4K from 66.3% to 66.2%. The principal degradation trend persists.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The benchmark definitions and effective-length rule based on 85% of the base score are retained.

C1.justification: The central benchmark contribution and claims about literal matching, latent reasoning, and degradation below advertised context limits remain. Updated model counts supply additional evidence. The abstract's added CoT/reasoning limitation was already stated in v2's introduction and Section 4.4.3.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds a qualified interpretation of newer models: GPT-4.1 improves effective context length to 16K but remains far below its claimed 1M, while GPT-4o remains relatively strong at 128K. The existing attention-based explanation and acknowledged need for deeper mechanistic study remain.

D1.justification: Table 8 supplies revision or checkpoint identifiers for the added models. Appendix E documents the extended-test constraints and specifies zero thinking budget for Gemini 2.5 Flash. Existing prompt templates, decoding settings for retained models, and the dataset/code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to Gemini (2023) and Gemma 3 (2025). The Gemini 1.5 report is retained under revised author naming. Positioning against NIAH and other literal-match benchmarks remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 removes a duplicated evaluation sentence, reorders contribution bullets, adds section cross-references, and clarifies filtering and word-order terminology. Appendices E–G extend the document, but the main narrative and section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 10–12 and the unsmoothed Figure 6, expands the model tables, and exchanges the numbering and placement of the earlier Figures 2 and 3. Captions, labels, and some placements are refined while retaining the existing visual design.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's 32K ceiling and limited model-specific hop breakdowns, v3 provides newer-model and 128K results, broader hop analyses, and raw depth curves in Tables 10–12 and Figure 6. These improve empirical relevance and transparency. The added long-context tests have reduced placement coverage, and the central mechanistic limitations remain, making this a useful but limited overall improvement.
